title: Implementing CBC in Your School: A Practical Guide (2026)
h1: Implementing CBC in Your School: A Practical Guide (2026)
description: How to implement CBC in a Kenyan school — plan coverage, capture rubrics and strands, report to parents, and support teachers through the transition.
author: SQUL Team
intro: The Competency-Based Curriculum changed what "good" looks like in a Kenyan classroom: from marks to competencies, from one exam to continuous assessment, from covering a syllabus to building skills. Implementing it well is a management job as much as a teaching one. This guide covers **CBC implementation in schools in Kenya**, part of our wider guide on [how to manage a school in Kenya](/blog/how-to-manage-a-school-in-kenya).
We focus on the practical: planning, capturing assessment, reporting to parents, and supporting teachers through the transition.

sections.heading: What CBC changes for a school

blocks.text: The management implication is records: CBC generates far more assessment data than a single exam, and it must be captured once, well, and reported clearly.

sections.heading: Planning coverage and schemes of work

items: **Map the strands** for each grade and subject at the start of term.
**Agree schemes of work** so teaching keeps pace across streams.
**Sequence assessment** — decide which strands are assessed when.
**Review weekly** — coverage drifts if it is not checked.

blocks.text: Good CBC assessment is captured at the point of observation, not reconstructed from memory at the end of term. Teachers record rubric levels — often exceeding, meeting, approaching, or below expectation — against each strand.

items: **Assess as you teach** — record strand-level observations during activities.
**Use consistent rubrics** across streams so reports are comparable.
**Capture once, digitally** — a spreadsheet per teacher guarantees inconsistencies.
**Review before reporting** — spot missing strands and gaps in time to fill them.

blocks.title: Capture, don't retype
blocks.text: A school management system with CBC assessment built in removes the end-of-term retyping that eats teaching time. See [CBC report card software in Kenya](/blog/cbc-report-card-software-kenya).

CBC reports are richer than a mark sheet, and parents find them harder to read. The school's job is to make them clear: competency levels per strand, a short teacher comment, and what the parent can do to help. Print-ready, consistent reports do more for parent trust than any newsletter.

Deliver reports on time over WhatsApp and SMS, and send notices parents will actually read — see [fee reminders over SMS and WhatsApp](/blog/school-fee-reminder-sms-whatsapp-kenya) for the messaging approach.

items: **Train on rubrics**, not just on the curriculum document.
**Peer observation** — teachers learn CBC design from each other.
**Share exemplars** — good assessment tasks spread fast.
**Protect time** — CBC assessment takes time; do not bury teachers in unrelated paperwork.

blocks.text: Kenyan schools currently run both models: CBC in the lower years and 8-4-4 in the upper secondary years (mid-transition). Manage both from one system so records agree. For the academic side, see [CBC report card software](/blog/cbc-report-card-software-kenya) and the [best school management software in Kenya](/blog/best-school-management-software-kenya).

items: **Assessment by memory** at term's end, instead of as you teach.
**Inconsistent rubrics** across streams, making reports incomparable.
**Paper-first capture** that has to be retyped into reports.
**Parents left in the dark** about how to read CBC reports.
**No time for teachers** — the curriculum suffocates under admin.

faqs.question: How do schools in Kenya implement CBC?
faqs.answer: By mapping strands per grade and subject, agreeing schemes of work, capturing rubric-based assessment continuously, and reporting competency levels to parents. Consistent rubrics and digital capture are what keep it manageable.

faqs.question: What are rubrics in CBC?
faqs.answer: Rubrics describe levels of competency — commonly exceeding, meeting, approaching, or below expectation — against each strand. Teachers record a level as learners demonstrate the skill.

faqs.question: Do Kenyan schools still use 8-4-4?
faqs.answer: Schools are mid-transition: CBC covers the lower grades while 8-4-4 applies to the upper secondary years. Good systems handle both so records stay consistent.

faqs.question: How do we report CBC to parents?
faqs.answer: With print-ready reports showing competency levels per strand and a short teacher comment, delivered on time over WhatsApp or SMS. Clarity builds parent trust.

faqs.question: Can software make CBC easier?
faqs.answer: Yes. Capturing rubrics and strands in a school management system removes end-of-term retyping and produces report cards directly. See our CBC report card guide.
